reasoning: Plan A is the better choice for an athlete aiming to become a faster trail runner. While both plans incorporate rest days, Plan A includes a variety of training types – aerobic, hill, and long runs – which are crucial for developing a well-rounded trail running skillset. Plan B focuses solely on easy runs, which, while important for building a base, won't sufficiently challenge the athlete to improve speed and strength on trails. The inclusion of hill work in Plan A is particularly valuable for trail running, as it directly addresses the demands of climbing and descending.
